project.title: When Governance Changes What Gets Counted: Measurement Validity for LLM Agent Evaluation

contract.gap: Runtime governance evaluations can use a condition written by the agent both to enforce a rule and to select the records used by a conditional rate.
contract.task: Evaluate this measurement-validity risk with paired WAGF simulations and define a reporting protocol that keeps the denominator and world-state dependence visible.
outcomes: prevalence of the agent-written scarcity condition

questions.text: Does enforcement change the prevalence of an agent-reported condition as well as the rate computed among those reports?
How much of the anchor contrast is descriptively associated with different simulator-recorded world states?
Which additional statistics remain interpretable when the denominator is fixed by design?

contract.contribution: A bounded measurement-validity risk and a low-cost reporting protocol for governed LLM-agent evaluations.
nonclaims: The paper does not claim deception or gaming.
The paper does not identify a causal effect of validation.
The paper does not identify a within-world reporting revision because the first response before retry is missing.
The paper does not claim universal behavior across agent frameworks.
The paper does not treat reweighting as a causal adjustment or corrected effect estimate.

semantic_locks.canonical: When Governance Changes What Gets Counted

discouraged_phrases: it is important to note that

alignment.method: Compare validator-on and validator-off prevalence and conditional rates in paired irrigation simulations.
alignment.evidence: Table 1 and the frozen irrigation evidence inventory report per-seed values and contrasts.
alignment.result: All five irrigation configurations have positive prevalence contrasts; the anchor conditional rate contrast is +23.02 percentage points.
alignment.interpretation: The conditional score and its selected population move together.
alignment.limitation: The first response before a retry is unavailable, so within-decision report revision is unresolved.
alignment.contribution: Shows why a conditional conformance score needs condition prevalence beside it.

alignment.method: Directly standardize prevalence to pooled simulator-recorded world-state distributions in the anchor irrigation cell.
alignment.evidence: Figure 2, Table 2, and the frozen world-state evidence files report pooled residuals, coverage, and per-seed diagnostics.
alignment.result: The pooled residual is -2.53 percentage points at full coverage and +0.21 at the finest reported stratification.
alignment.interpretation: Different recorded-world composition is consistent with much of the raw prevalence contrast.
alignment.limitation: World state is downstream of governance, so the decomposition is descriptive rather than causal.
alignment.contribution: Separates a supported world-state composition diagnosis from an unsupported causal claim.

alignment.method: Compare the conditional increase rate with an all-decision rate using the same final-action reading.
alignment.evidence: Figure 3 and the frozen consequence evidence report contrasts for all five irrigation configurations.
alignment.result: The fixed-denominator contrast can be near zero or reverse sign relative to the conditional contrast.
alignment.interpretation: The denominator is part of the estimand, not a formatting detail.
alignment.limitation: The fixed-denominator rate answers a different question and is not presented as an automatic correction.
alignment.contribution: Provides a low-cost reporting protocol for governed-agent evaluations.
